summary.text: A 17-year-old previously healthy female patient presented to the emergency department on 25 October 2024 with one day of worsening right iliac fossa pain, pallor and dizziness. She was tachycardic, normotensive and afebrile with signs of an acute abdomen. Blood tests showed pancytopenia, and CT showed moderate hemoperitoneum with an enlarged heterogeneous left ovary.

She received transfusion with partial improvement, and diagnostic laparoscopy confirmed a ruptured, actively bleeding left ovarian cyst with 400 mL hemoperitoneum, treated with washout and diathermy. After ICU admission she was discharged six days later with ongoing cytopenias. Follow-up showed persistent anemia and thrombocytopenia with transfusion dependence.

Further workup found a minor PNH clone on flow cytometry, a severely hypocellular marrow without dysplasia, fibrosis or malignancy, and no pathogenic variants on the myeloid NGS panel. She was diagnosed with aplastic anemia with a subclinical PNH clone and commenced on anti-thymocyte globulin, cyclosporin and eltrombopag; an allogeneic transplant was scheduled for September 2025. She is currently receiving immunosuppressive therapy while awaiting the transplant.

She re-presented three months later with epigastric and periumbilical pain, and CT confirmed active hemoperitoneum due to right ovarian bleeding. A second diagnostic laparoscopy revealed a ruptured corpus luteum, treated with diathermy and evacuation. After discussion with hematology she started monthly goserelin for ovulation suppression and combined hormone replacement therapy with Evorel.
